title: Divers Found 'Corpses' at the Bottom of the Sea in 1900. It Was Something Far Stranger.
description:
In October 1900, a sponge diver off the Greek island of Antikythera surfaced screaming about a pile of corpses on the seafloor — but what his crew found was a 2,000-year-old Roman shipwreck loaded with bronze statues, coins, and glass. Two divers were paralyzed and one died recovering the treasure, victims of a disease no one yet understood: the bends.

Among the wreckage sat a blackened, corroded lump the size of a shoebox, ignored in a museum for months until archaeologist Valerios Stais spotted a gear embedded in the rock. Decades of X-ray analysis later, researchers uncovered 30 interlocking bronze gears — an ancient mechanical computer capable of predicting eclipses, tracking the moon's wobble, and mapping the Olympic calendar.

Nothing this precise would be built again for over a thousand years. There are no blueprints, no matching workshop, and no second device — just 82 fragments and a question that still haunts historians: who had the knowledge to build this, and how was it lost?
